package_info.package_name: Azure Key Vault Contributor Role (misconfiguration abuse)
package_info.package_versions: All versions of the Key Vault Contributor role when used with access policy-based Key Vaults
package_info.why_malicious: The Key Vault Contributor role, when assigned to a user on a Key Vault configured with access policies, allows the user to escalate privileges by modifying access policies to grant themselves full data access. This violates the intended boundary of the role, which is not supposed to allow access to secrets, keys, or certificates, and enables privilege escalation and unauthorized data access.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon user interaction via Azure Portal, CLI, or API)
execution_context.file_location: Azure Resource Manager API / Azure Portal / Azure CLI

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: az keyvault set-policy --name <vault-name> --object-id <attacker-object-id> --secret-permissions get list set delete --key-permissions get list --certificate-permissions get list
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code modifies the access policy of a target Key Vault to grant the attacker's principal full permissions to secrets, keys, and certificates, enabling subsequent data access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Granting oneself broad access to sensitive data by modifying access policies is a classic privilege escalation technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, the Key Vault Contributor role should not allow data access to secrets, keys, or certificates. Here, the user bypasses this restriction by changing access policies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Administrators may legitimately update access policies to grant access to service principals or users as part of onboarding or automation.
key_indicators: Self-assignment of all data plane permissions
Modification of access policies by non-administrative users
Use of Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/write or accessPolicies/write to escalate privileges

execution_context.file_location: Azure Resource Manager API / Azure Portal / Azure CLI

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
az keyvault secret list --vault-name <vault-name>
az keyvault secret show --vault-name <vault-name> --name <secret-name>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After modifying access policies, the code lists and retrieves all secrets from the target Key Vault, exfiltrating sensitive data such as API keys, passwords, and certificates.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing all secrets immediately after a self-assigned policy change is highly indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal users with the Key Vault Contributor role should not be able to read secrets; this is only possible due to the prior privilege escalation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate users with explicit data access may list and retrieve secrets for application configuration.
key_indicators: Temporal proximity to access policy changes
Access from accounts not previously authorized for data plane operations

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises a user account with the Key Vault Contributor role.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to manage Key Vault resources but not data access (initially).

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/write permission to modify the Key Vault's access policies, granting themselves full data access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker's principal now has data plane permissions to secrets, keys, and certificates.

attack_chain.action: Attacker enumerates and retrieves all secrets, keys, and certificates from the Key Vault.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data (API keys, passwords, certificates, etc.)

behavioral_signatures: Modification of Key Vault access policies by users with only Contributor-level roles
Self-assignment of broad data plane permissions (get, list, set, delete) to new principals
Immediate access to secrets/keys/certificates following access policy changes
file_indicators: No specific files; monitor Azure Resource Manager activity logs for access policy changes
Audit logs showing az keyvault set-policy or equivalent API calls
network_indicators: Azure Resource Manager API calls to Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/write and accessPolicies/write
Subsequent calls to Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/secrets/read, keys/read, certificates/read
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Azure Activity Logs for access policy modifications on Key Vaults, especially by users with the Key Vault Contributor role. Correlate these events with subsequent data access operations (listing or retrieving secrets, keys, or certificates) by the same principal. Alert on cases where a user grants themselves new data plane permissions and immediately accesses sensitive data. Regularly audit Key Vault access policies for unexpected or unauthorized principals.
